events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 1103 AM EDT, A combination of NJDOT, automated rain gauges, and
media reports indicated flash flooding is ongoing with extensive
flooding being reported in the Highlands area of NJ and portions of
both North and South Brunswick have reported road closures. Doppler
radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain across portions
of the warned area. Between 1 and 4 inches of rain have fallen
already with additional rainfall of up to 2 inches possible. For the
coastal communities this rainfall is combining with increasing high
tides to produce significant flooding. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets, and underpasses.

Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Trenton, New Brunswick, Perth Amboy, Long Branch, Sandy Hook,
Somerset, Edison, Middletown, Old Bridge, East Brunswick, South
Brunswick and Sayreville.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 295 in New Jersey between mile markers 55 and 76.
New Jersey Turnpike between exits 7 and 13.
Interstate 287 in New Jersey between mile markers 0 and 11.
Interstate 195 in New Jersey between mile markers 0 and 20.
Garden State Parkway between mile markers 106 and 134.

events.region: Western Columbia River Gorge in Oregon and Washington
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS EXPECTED IN THE SOUTHERN
WILLAMETTE VALLEY MONDAY AFTERNOON AND EVENING DUE TO DRY
CONDITIONS AND NORTHERLY WINDS GUSTING UP TO 25 MPH...

...CRITICAL FIRE WEATHER CONDITIONS EXPECTED IN THE WESTERN
COLUMBIA RIVER GORGE TUESDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH WEDNESDAY EVENING
FOR DRY CONDITIONS AND EASTERLY WINDS UP TO 40 MPH...

The National Weather Service in Portland has issued a Red Flag
Warning for wind and low relative humidity, which is in effect
from 11 AM Tuesday to 8 PM PDT Wednesday. The Fire Weather Watch
is no longer in effect.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Washington, Fire Weather Zone 636 Western
Columbia River Gorge in Oregon and Washington.

* WINDS...East 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 40 mph. Winds will be
strongest Tuesday morning through early Tuesday afternoon, and
again Tuesday night through early Wednesday afternoon.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 15-20 percent. Relative humidity
values will be lowest Tuesday afternoon and Wednesday afternoon.
Poor overnight humidity recoveries are expected Tuesday night
with maximum relative humidity values ranging between 35-45%.

* IMPACTS...Conditions may be favorable for rapid fire spread
which may threaten life and property. Use extra caution with
potential ignition sources, especially in grassy areas.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.

events.region: Beaverhead, MT; Deer Lodge, MT; Flathead, MT; Granite, MT; Lake, MT; Lincoln, MT; Mineral, MT; Missoula, MT; Ravalli, MT; Sanders, MT; Silver Bow, MT
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
AQAMT

The Montana Department of Environmental Quality has issued an air
quality alert for Flathead, Lake, Lincoln, Beaverhead, Sanders, Deer
Lodge, Silver Bow, Granite, Mineral, Sanders, and Missoula counties
in effect until 9AM on 08/04/2026
An Air Quality Alert means that particulates have been trending
upwards and that an exceedance of the 24 hour National Ambient Air
Quality Standard (NAAQS) has occurred or may occur in the near
future.

Elevated particulate levels from wildfire smoke

As of 6AM on 08/03/2026, particulate levels in Billings, Columbia
Falls, Frenchtown, Lewistown, Libby, Missoula and Thompson Falls are
Unhealthy.

As of 6AM on 08/03/2026, particulate levels in Butte are Unhealthy
for Sensitive Groups.

As of 6AM on 08/03/2026, particulate levels in Dillon, Great Falls,
Hamilton, Helena, Malta and Sleeping Giant are Moderate.

When air quality is Unhealthy... State and local health officials
recommend that people with respiratory or heart disease, the elderly,
and children should avoid prolonged exertion; everyone else should
limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups... State and local
health officials recommend that people with respiratory or heart
disease, the elderly and children should limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Moderate... State and local health officials
recommend that unusually sensitive people should consider reducing
prolonged or heavy exertion.

For more information visit the Montana Department of Environmental
Quality at http://todaysair.mtdeq.us

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...Until Thursday afternoon.

roads are closed. Airport Road boat ramp near Live Oak County
Airport is flooded and closed. Major flooding occurs in the River
Creek Acres Subdivision, with several feet of water and several
homes flooded. Residents in the J.I. Hailey Subdivision at Jones
River bend have trouble getting out as water covers much of
Antelope Lane.

- At 8:15 AM CDT Monday the stage was 37.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall into moderate flood
stage Tuesday, then fall below flood stage midday Thursday. The
river will then continue to fall to 12.8 feet Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
